transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, D.C., I'm Dale Willman.
Three judges from the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals held an unusual Sunday hearing
at the Department of Justice's lawsuit against California over its voter rolls.
As NPR's Drew Joffe Block reports, the DOJ is trying to demand election officials set
aside the ballots of 20,000 registered voters.
The DOJ says the registered voters in question are likely non-citizens and is arguing that
California election officials must be stopped from processing their ballots.
Lawyers for the state in Los Angeles County have argued that the DOJ's list is unreliable
and doing what the federal government demands would be unlawful and logistically infeasible
at this point.
A federal judge set a hearing in the case for this Tuesday, but before that could happen,
the DOJ appealed to the Ninth Circuit, arguing the lower court wasn't moving fast enough.
In the Sunday hearing, two of the three judges on the panel had hard questions for the DOJ
attorney, both about the department's demands and whether the appeals court can even weigh
in at this stage.
Drew Joffe Block, NPR News.
>> Flavio Bolsonaro is refusing to concede defeat in Brazil's presidential runoff election
Sunday.
Incumbent Luis Anacio Lula da Silva beat Bolsonaro by more than 4 million votes.
But Bolsonaro, heard through a BBC interpreter, says he's not done fighting.
>> What I have to say now is this is impossible.
It's impossible to recognize the election results in the context of how it unfolded.
We will take the risk of asking to annul these elections.
>> There was some disruption in Sunday's voting as both candidates asked that polls remain
open longer because of poor weather and transportation issues.
A shooting near the Florida A&M University Stadium Saturday following the school's homecoming
football game left 12 people injured including six children.
Now as students head back to class Monday, the university says it's focused on helping
its students heal and looking toward the future.
Regan McCarthy of member station WFSU has more.
>> FAMU president Marva Johnson says counseling will be available for students to help them
work through trauma following the event.
In a video posted on social media, Johnson points out the incident took place off campus,
but she says healing will happen as a university.
>> We are a family at FAMU and our pride, our identity and our future will not be defined
by the challenges we face, but how we respond to them together.
>> Johnson says she's grateful for the law enforcement officers who responded quickly
to the incident and who are now leading the ongoing investigation.
No arrests have been made.
For NPR news, I'm Regan McCarthy in Tallahassee.
>> Asian stocks closed down on Monday, echoing losses Friday on Wall Street.
Japan's Nikkei dipped eight tenths, while South Korea's market fell by four tenths.
It has shed almost 19% so far just this month.
You're listening to NPR news.
Prices are high this Halloween, but the National Retail Federation finds Americans are still
spending on the holiday, on average around $115 each.
>> At the same time, they're also looking for ways to cut back, and PR's Amy Held reports.
>> After candy, then decorations, costumes are the third biggest purchase.
But what's scary is how fast they haunt a landfill.
>> We're spending billions on something we wear for one night and creating all of this
waste.
>> Lexi Silverstein is a sustainable fashion advocate in California.
>> Most costumes are made from polyester, which is basically plastic.
>> That breaks down, polluting the environment.
>> Halloween started the ultimate Halloween swap, recycling hundreds of costumes last
year in LA and Baltimore.
It's expanding.
>> This is about communities helping each other, and if there isn't a swap near you,
start one.
>> The National Retail Federation finds a third of consumers are seeking Halloween stuff
that can be resurrected.
Amy Held, NPR News.
>> Security forces in Jordan say they've arrested three men for an attack on a Greek Orthodox
Church Friday that killed nine people and wounded more than two dozen others.
Individuals say the three suspects were arrested after a shootout in which they were all wounded.
>> The musical "Rent" is having a Broadway party Monday to celebrate its 30th anniversary.
A special performance of the show will be held at the Richard Rogers Theater, and it
will include several of the original cast members.
Proceeds will be given to charity.
The musical has won multiple Tony Awards, as well as a Pulitzer Prize.
Its creator, Jonathan Larson, died in 1996 before seeing its success.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Ninth Circuit judges hear DOJ lawsuit over California voter rolls and 20,000 ballots in unusual Sunday hearing
Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro refuses to concede to Lula da Silva after presidential runoff loss
Florida A&M University offers counseling after Saturday shooting near campus injures 12, including six children
Asian stocks close lower Monday, following Wall Street losses Friday; Japan's Nikkei dips 0.8%
Americans spending on Halloween costumes, with swaps growing to reduce polyester waste
Jordan arrests three men over attack on Greek Orthodox church that killed nine
Broadway celebrates 30th anniversary of musical Rent with special charity performance
